column1: # Let's begin. This file specifies the different parameters that can be changed by the user and are read by the relay Arduinos. It can be generated by a Windows application that can be found here: https://github.com/flipoyo/MOLO-firmware-config or you can change the parameters using Notepad :)

# The appEui is the unique identifier of the relay whereas the devEui is the unique identifier of the datalogger. It is used to establish a connection between the dataloggers and the relays (so that a relay can know which datalogger to communicate with when there are many).

# These values are either hardcoded into the Arduino by the manufacturer or can be generated randomly (such that they respect the EUI constraints (16 base-16 / hex characters)) by the Windows application on GitHub. We haven't tried the generated EUIs due to time constraints but it should work in theory provided that the server/receiver has these values in its configuration files as well.

column2: we have to insert them according to the `datalogger_slot` index in the datalogger's config file. For example
column3: in the config file of the datalogger "a8610a34334d710d"
column4: datalogger_slot is 0 so it is inserted first.

column1: # This indicates the system's cycle duration. This means that every 240s
column2: the relay will start communicating with all the sensors sequentially. Each datalogger will communicate with the relay during the `time_window` specified below. The rest of the time will be dedicated to sending the data from the relay to the server.
